newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Largest Kazakh oil company says H1 output flat.
newsitem.headline: Largest Kazakh oil company says H1 output flat.

text.p: Kazakhstan's largest oil producer, Mangistaumunaigaz, produced 2.24 million tonnes of oil in the first half of this year, or about 89,000 barrels per day (bpd), nudging up a mere 0.8 percent on last year's level.
The firm, which sits on recoverable reserves of 314.6 million tonnes, produced 500,000 bpd in the Soviet era.
Indonesia's Central Asia Petroleum Ltd has a 60 percent stake in Mangistaumunaigaz.

Central Asia, part-owned by Indonesia's PT Medco Energy Corp and Sedtco Group, has pledged an investment of $4.1 billion, including $2 billion in the first five years. The Indonesian firm plans to at least double Mangistau's oil output in the next five years.

Kazakhstan -- a vast Central Asian state with oil reserves estimated in the billions of tonnes -- plans to increase its total oil production to 27 million tonnes (540,000 bpd) this year from 23 million tonnes (460,000 bpd) in 1996. It plans to produce 170 million tonnes (3.4 million bpd) by 2010.
